module-4-customer-cleanup-project.label: Module 4 Customer Cleanup Project
module-4-customer-cleanup-project.summary: Build one data-quality report that starts with missing emails, narrows to inactive follow-ups, and finishes with real H-city records.

mp_3.title: Publish the real H-city cleanup queue

mp-1-find-missing-emails.title: Flag missing-email records
mp-1-find-missing-emails.prompt: Data operations needs the first cleanup slice. Return `id`, `full_name`, and `email` from `customers`, in that order, keeping only rows where `email` is missing.
mp-1-find-missing-emails.hint: The starter uses the opposite NULL condition; change it so missing values remain.

help.concept: Missing values are tested with IS NULL.
help.hint_1: Keep the selected columns and table unchanged.
help.hint_2: Change only the NULL condition so the result keeps missing emails.

mp-1-find-missing-emails.starterCode:
-- The current NULL check keeps present emails. Fix it to keep missing emails.
SELECT
  id,
  full_name,
  email
FROM customers
WHERE email IS NOT NULL;
mp-1-find-missing-emails.solutionCode:
SELECT
  id,
  full_name,
  email
FROM customers
WHERE email IS NULL;

sourceChecks.message: Use the `customers` table in the FROM clause.
Select the required columns in the requested order: `id`, `full_name`, `email`.

mp-2-keep-real-follow-ups.title: Narrow to inactive follow-ups
mp-2-keep-real-follow-ups.prompt: The support team will follow up only on inactive customers from the approved missing-email slice. Return `id`, `full_name`, `email`, and `status`, in that order, while preserving the missing-email requirement.
mp-2-keep-real-follow-ups.hint: Keep the working missing-email filter and add one exact status requirement that must also be true.

help.concept: A cumulative project extends the working filter instead of replacing it.
help.hint_1: Do not replace the earlier missing-email rule.
help.hint_2: Add status to the result and narrow the rows to inactive customers.

mp-2-keep-real-follow-ups.starterCode:
SELECT
  id,
  full_name,
  email
FROM customers
WHERE email IS NULL;
mp-2-keep-real-follow-ups.solutionCode:
SELECT
  id,
  full_name,
  email,
  status
FROM customers
WHERE email IS NULL
  AND status = 'inactive';

sourceChecks.message: Use the `customers` table in the FROM clause.

mp-3-finish-cleanup-report.title: Publish the real H-city cleanup queue
mp-3-finish-cleanup-report.prompt: Before handoff, operations wants only real customer records from cities beginning with `H`. Return `id`, `full_name`, `email`, `city`, and `status`, in that order. Preserve the missing-email and inactive-customer requirements, keep only H-city records, and exclude test rows.
mp-3-finish-cleanup-report.hint: Keep every approved condition, add a prefix text filter for city, and use the `is_test` flag so only real records remain.

help.concept: The final report combines missing-value, exact-value, text-pattern, and test-record rules.
help.hint_2: In this dataset, `0` in `is_test` represents a real record.

mp-3-finish-cleanup-report.starterCode:
SELECT
  id,
  full_name,
  email,
  status
FROM customers
WHERE email IS NULL
  AND status = 'inactive';
mp-3-finish-cleanup-report.solutionCode:
SELECT
  id,
  full_name,
  email,
  city,
  status
FROM customers
WHERE email IS NULL
  AND status = 'inactive'
  AND city LIKE 'H%'
  AND is_test = 0;

sketch_project_brief.title: Project brief
sketch_project_brief.bodyMarkdown:
The data-operations team is cleaning a customer follow-up list before it goes to support.

Start by identifying records with no stored email. Support then narrows that approved result to inactive customers who need a different follow-up channel. Before the final handoff, operations wants only real customer records from cities beginning with `H`, with test rows excluded.

Build one query through three milestones. Each milestone should preserve the working rules from the previous step and add only the newly approved requirement.
